## Findings
- claim-1: For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), Theorem 5.4 gives two generating families indexed respectively by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\) and \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\); each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The paper conjectures that both families are minimal and reports computer verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1495-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: For the first unreported corner instance \((r,n-r,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\), one has \((a,b,N)=(3,2,10)\). The specialized families are \[ F_1=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55), \quad F_2=(22,221,2211,222,22111,2221,22211,2222,22221,22222). \] [artifact e043e3963e2ca3b2a6e531559996e6fdfaf60f0cfcc274c9b277a5a207cc26fc]
- claim-4: The attempted degree-block unit-pivot certificate for this instance fails for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\), first in degree \(7\); thus this computation neither supports nor refutes minimality. It obstructs only this proposed certificate method. [artifact e043e3963e2ca3b2a6e531559996e6fdfaf60f0cfcc274c9b277a5a207cc26fc]
- claim-5: The stronger statement \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) was explicitly only suspected by the authors, who state that a proof eluded them. [source-2@L1547-L1552|claim=formal-document]
## Strategy
Separate source-backed statements: the two families generate \(J_v\), minimality is conjectural, and verification is reported for \(r\le4,\ q\le5\). Treat \(i=j=1\) and certified boundary computations as supporting internal examples only. Treat \((5,6,2,2)\) as unresolved because the supplied computational records conflict.

## Gaps
No new independently implemented computation for a case outside the reported range is supplied. The alleged degree-\(7\) pivot failure is invalidated by the critic’s echelon-invariant objection and cannot obstruct minimality. No counterexample is established.

## Next
Compute a fresh unreported case, distinct from \((5,6,2,2)\), using an independently written exact Smith-form or unimodular-minor certificate. Classify its result only as supporting, refuting, or inconclusive after verifying the full relation lattice integrally.
